messages:
maya: quick summary - ran a multi-region kv-cache microbench across h100/a100 with 3 seqlen buckets (128/512/2048). observed hit-rate collapse above ~1k for eu-west a100 which correlates with p99 token latency spikes. wondering if eviction policy or kernel selection is amplifying page-in tail. any guesses?
oliver: can you paste the numbers? what eviction policy was used for that run?
maya: policy was baseline LRU with async prefetch disabled, eviction threshold = 0.6 (cache fill fraction). link to perf dump: https://perf.internal/runs/185412
oliver: quick paste from the run (us-east / eu-west, h100 / a100):
- seqlen=128: hit 98.6% / 98.1%, p50 12ms / 14ms, p99 34ms / 40ms
- seqlen=512: hit 94.2% / 92.8%, p50 18ms / 22ms, p99 78ms / 120ms
- seqlen=2048: hit 76.1% / 58.3%, p50 45ms / 85ms, p99 220ms / 560ms
raj: wow that p99 jump on eu-west a100 at 2048 is huge. likely paging + kernel fallback. eu-west nodes have slightly older firmware + different kernel build (we still have an older cuKernel patch there).
perf-bot: automated-run summary:
```
run_id,region,gpu,seqlen,hit_rate,p50_ms,p99_ms,evictions
185412.1,us-east,h100,2048,76.1,45,220,18234
185412.2,eu-west,a100,2048,58.3,85,560,34102
```
perf-bot: attached full flamegraphs -> https://perf.internal/artifacts/185412/flame
sophia: two quick angles:
1) try size-aware eviction (segment by kv entry size + freq) instead of pure LRU. reduces thrash for large seqs.
2) enable async prefetcher on a small fraction (10% of requests) to warm KV cache for long context traces.
sophia: config snippet to try:
```
cache.eviction.policy = "segmented-lru"
cache.eviction.size_threshold = 0.7
prefetch.async_fraction = 0.1
prefetch.max_parallel = 4
```
infra-bot: note: eu-west a100 pool currently at 85% reserved commit; autoscaler has 6–8m cold-start on new nodes for that SKU. if test spikes, we may hit capacity fallback to smaller instances which hurts kernel perf.
oliver: another useful check is kernel selection logs (we log selected kernel id per batch). grep for `kernel_selector` in trace, see whether it switches to fallback path when memory pressure is high.
oliver: quick CLI to re-run bench with tracer + kernel logs:
```
redwood-bench run --region eu-west --gpu a100 --seqlen 2048 --runs 200 \
  --cache-policy segmented-lru --enable-prefetch true \
  --trace kernel_selector,kv_paging --out /tmp/185412-eu-a100
```
maya: can you prioritize that in next maintenance window? capture kernel_selector + page-in latency histograms. also please run same on us-east h100 for parity.
raj: ack - I'll queue it for tonight (ETA ~22:00 UTC). will pin config and upload artifacts to the perf link above.
sophia: also add synthetic tail traces (bursty long seqs) to exercise worst-case page-ins. they reveal whether increasing prefetch fraction helps p99 without dropping overall hit-rate.
maya: perfect. thanks team — let's reconvene after the run. i'll open a follow-up doc with the expected evaluation matrix (seqlen buckets, eviction configs, prefetch fractions, kernel variants) and tag this thread. :thumbsup:
